survey: A spiral-clipped topiary shrub in a round raised bed edged with stone. The shrub is four stacked tiers that get smaller toward the top. Each tier is offset slightly from the one below, so together they read as a spiral coil. The top is a small rounded crown. The lowest and widest tier sits in dark soil inside the stone ring and overhangs the edge slightly, as a full shrub would. The stone ring sits flat on the lawn, and its segments join into a continuous circle in correct perspective. The whole shrub rests on the bed and leans only slightly, well within what a living, clipped plant can do. No central trunk shows between the coils. Real game cards often simplify topiary this way, and it does not make the plant implausible. Nothing floats, nothing is a loose end, nothing is invented, and the bed ring is round.
